1.prerequisites: count valence electrons from the periodic table, tell ionic from covalent bonding, and use the electronegativity trend (CHEM 3A).

readiness.q: How many valence electrons does a nitrogen atom have?
Which bond is more polar, C–H or O–H?
readiness.a: O–H. The electronegativity difference between O and H is much larger than between C and H.

readiness.q: Is NaCl held together by ionic or covalent bonding?
readiness.a: Ionic. Sodium transfers an electron to chlorine, giving Na<sup>+</sup> and Cl<sup>−</sup> ions.

2.prerequisites: draw Lewis structures in which carbon makes four bonds and explain London dispersion forces (Chapter 1).

readiness.q: How many bonds does carbon make in a neutral molecule?
In the Lewis structure of CH<sub>4</sub>, how many bonding pairs and lone pairs are on carbon, and what is the shape?
readiness.a: Four bonding pairs and no lone pairs; tetrahedral, with bond angles of about 109.5°.

readiness.q: Which has the higher boiling point, CH<sub>4</sub> or C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub>? Why?
readiness.a: C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub>. The larger molecule has stronger London dispersion forces.

3.prerequisites: name straight-chain and branched alkanes and recognize structural isomers (Chapter 2).

readiness.q: Name CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub>.
How many hydrogen atoms are in a saturated alkane with five carbons?
Are CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>CH<sub>3</sub> and CH<sub>3</sub>CH(CH<sub>3</sub>)CH<sub>3</sub> the same compound or isomers?
readiness.a: Structural isomers: both are C<sub>4</sub>H<sub>10</sub>, but the atoms are connected differently.

4.prerequisites: recognize hydrogen bonding (Chapter 1), name a parent chain (Chapter 2), and predict the product of hydration of an alkene (Chapter 3).

readiness.q: Which can hydrogen-bond with itself, CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH or CH<sub>3</sub>OCH<sub>3</sub>?
readiness.a: Ethanol, CH<sub>3</sub>CH<sub>2</sub>OH. It has an H on oxygen; dimethyl ether does not.

readiness.q: What forms when water adds across the C=C of ethene (acid catalyst)?
What parent name is used for a continuous chain of three carbons?

5.prerequisites: classify alcohols as 1°, 2° or 3° and predict what oxidation of each gives (Chapter 4).

readiness.q: Is 2-propanol a 1°, 2° or 3° alcohol?
readiness.a: 2°: the carbon bearing the OH is bonded to two other carbons.

readiness.q: What does oxidation of a 2° alcohol give?
Can a 3° alcohol be oxidized by the usual oxidizing agents?
readiness.a: No. The carbon bearing the OH has no hydrogen to lose.

6.prerequisites: predict the oxidation products of 1° alcohols and aldehydes (Chapters 4–5) and write a neutralization (CHEM 3A).

readiness.q: What does complete oxidation of ethanol give?
readiness.a: Acetic acid (ethanoic acid), by way of acetaldehyde.

readiness.q: What are the products when an acid reacts with NaOH?
Which functional group has a C=O with a hydrogen on the carbonyl carbon?

7.prerequisites: use the Brønsted–Lowry definition of a base (CHEM 3A) and write esterification (Chapter 6).

readiness.q: A Brønsted–Lowry base is a proton ______.
Which two compounds react, with an acid catalyst and heat, to form an ester?
readiness.a: A carboxylic acid and an alcohol; water is released.

readiness.q: What forms when ammonia, NH<sub>3</sub>, accepts an H<sup>+</sup>?

8.prerequisites: recognize aldehydes, ketones and hemiacetals and identify a chiral carbon (Chapter 5).

readiness.q: What forms when an alcohol adds to the C=O of an aldehyde?
What makes a carbon atom chiral?
readiness.a: It has four different groups attached.

readiness.q: Which gives a positive Tollens’ test, an aldehyde or a simple ketone?

9.prerequisites: write ester hydrolysis and saponification (Chapter 6), tell polar from nonpolar molecules (Chapter 1), and recognize cis and trans double bonds (Chapter 3).

readiness.q: What are the products of hydrolyzing an ester with NaOH?
readiness.a: A carboxylate salt and an alcohol (saponification).

readiness.q: Is a long hydrocarbon chain polar or nonpolar? Does it dissolve in water?
readiness.a: Nonpolar; it does not dissolve in water.

readiness.q: In a cis double bond, are the two chain parts on the same side or opposite sides?

10.prerequisites: recognize amines, carboxylic acids and amides (Chapters 6–7) and relate pH to whether a group holds or loses H<sup>+</sup>.

readiness.q: At pH 7, is a carboxylic acid group mostly –COOH or –COO<sup>−</sup>?
At pH 7, is a typical amine group mostly –NH<sub>2</sub> or –NH<sub>3</sub><sup>+</sup>?
readiness.a: –NH3+. The pKa of its protonated form (about 9–11) is above 7.

readiness.q: What bond forms when an amine reacts with a carboxylic acid (with heat)?

11.prerequisites: describe the levels of protein structure and denaturation (Chapter 10) and explain what a catalyst does (CHEM 3A).

readiness.q: What does a catalyst do to the activation energy of a reaction?
readiness.a: It lowers it. The overall energy change of the reaction stays the same.

readiness.q: Which level of protein structure is the sequence of amino acids?
What happens to a protein’s shape when it is heated strongly?
readiness.a: It denatures: the secondary and tertiary structure unfold, but the peptide bonds stay intact.

12.prerequisites: recognize ribose and deoxyribose (Chapter 8), hydrogen bonding (Chapter 1) and peptide bonds (Chapter 10).

readiness.q: Which five-carbon sugar is in RNA?
What attractions hold the two strands of DNA together?
What kind of bond links the amino acids in a protein?

13.prerequisites: draw glucose (Chapter 8), name the enzyme classes (Chapter 11) and define oxidation and reduction as loss or gain of hydrogen.

readiness.q: In biochemistry, is a molecule that gains hydrogen atoms oxidized or reduced?
Which enzyme class includes kinases, which move a phosphate from ATP onto another molecule?
What is the molecular formula of glucose?

14.prerequisites: list the products of glycolysis and the roles of NAD<sup>+</sup>, FAD and ATP (Chapter 13).

readiness.q: What does glycolysis produce (net) from one glucose?
Which is the reduced form, NAD<sup>+</sup> or NADH?
Without enough oxygen, what does muscle convert pyruvate into?

15.prerequisites: count ATP from acetyl CoA, NADH and FADH<sub>2</sub> with the course values (Chapter 14) and draw fatty acids (Chapter 9) and amino acids (Chapter 10).

readiness.q: How many ATP does one acetyl CoA give through the citric acid cycle and electron transport (course values)?
Is palmitic acid (16 carbons, no C=C) saturated or unsaturated?
Which element is found in amino acids but not in carbohydrates or fats?
